result.title: SWORD: Scene-Grounded Wasserstein Object-Relation Distance for 3D Scene Graph Prediction
result.summary: 3D scene graph prediction is commonly optimized with object-node and relation-edge classification losses. These objectives encourage exact object and relation label recovery, but they do not directly optimize semantic proximity to the ground-truth scene graph: two wrong graphs can receive comparable penalties even when one is much closer in object roles and relation contexts. A direct graph-distance loss is difficult in general, since graph matching and graph edit distance require correspondence search and edit-cost design. Our key observation is that prior supervised 3D scene graph prediction protocols are conducted on fixed object-node indices and supervised edge slots. This can turn a scene graph comparison into a well-defined aligned graph-distance problem. To this end, we propose SWORD, a Scene-Grounded Wasserstein Object-Relation Distance that builds block-normalized object and relation ground distance metrics from training scene graph annotations through a deterministic base-to-context order, without external semantic priors. SWORD lifts these metrics to Wasserstein distances over aligned node and null-augmented edge marginals, providing semantic graph-distance supervision beyond exact-label penalties while preserving the ground-truth graph as the unique zero-distance solution in aligned marginal probability space. We prove that SWORD is a strict metric on aligned marginal probabilistic scene graphs, preserves scene-graph-grounded substitution ordering, controls additive graph-grounded semantic observables, and yields a surrogate upper-bounding decoded semantic error.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SWORD，利用固定节点索引与边槽位的对齐设定，从训练标注构建物体与关系的地面距离度量，并将其提升为节点及零增强边边缘分布上的 Wasserstein 距离，作为 3D 场景图预测的语义图距离监督，替代仅靠精确标签的分类损失。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在无需图匹配的前提下比较对齐结构化表示分布」的 Wasserstein 距离构造，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态或轨迹的相似度度量与训练监督提供可核查的方法线索，但原文面向 3D 场景图标签预测，与视觉推理状态生成无直接联系。
